data.name: WooCommerce.WizardStepPrepBody
data.value:
Before connecting Tracker, configure your WordPress / WooCommerce store:

1. Use HTTPS for the store URL.
2. In WordPress, set Settings → Permalinks to a pretty permalink structure (not Plain) so the REST API works.
3. Recommended: create a dedicated WordPress user for Tracker (for example qtracker-api) with Administrator or Shop Manager role. Do not use a personal staff login for the API key — if that person leaves or the account is deleted/disabled, the key usually stops working.
4. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API and click Add key.
5. Description: e.g. QTracker_Integration. User: select the dedicated integration user (not your day-to-day login). Permissions: Read/Write.
6. If Woo shows User is missing, clear and re-select the user from the list, then generate the key again.
7. Copy the Consumer key and Consumer secret (the secret is shown only once).
8. Note your store base URL (example: https://shop.example.com) with no trailing path.
9. Optional: note the wp-admin base URL used to open orders in Woo (example: https://shop.example.com/wp-admin).

When you continue, Tracker will create companion database tables (orders and items tables are not altered).

data.name: WooCommerce.MapCatHelp
data.value: Pull categories from Woo, tick Include as needed, set All vs Included only, then Save includes. Unticked categories (e.g. Referral) are excluded from Mappings and Missing SKUs — even if mode is still All. Child categories are indented. S/O and Import defaults apply to unmapped products. Import "(inherit)" uses the parent category's Import setting — it is not the same as "Parent → order notes". Set the root (e.g. Gear) to Parent → order notes so children on (inherit) pick that up. Uncategorized is off by default when other categories exist.

data.name: WooCommerce.MapAttrParentsHelp
data.value: Each Woo attribute can feed Tracker order lines. Item (SKU) comes from product mapping. Here set cascades: Qty source / Pack source / Notes (1 = try first, 2 = if that is missing/Any). Coffee example: Packaging = Qty 1 + Pack 2; Prep Type = Pack 1. Save → Variant attributes → map option values → refresh Mappings. Order import will use the same resolve rules.

data.name: WooCommerce.MapAttrOptionsHelp
data.value: Map each Woo option to Tracker values. Sets is fixed by Attribute parents ranks. Packaging options: qty (and pack if Pack source is set). Prep options: Tracker packaging (grind codes like GrndPlng — Tracker still stores grind on packaging). Prefer (all types) only; re-pull after changing ranks.

data.name: WooCommerce.MapMapHelp
data.value: Applied shows check when stored, pencil if dirty, dash if not saved. Item/SKU is chosen here. Qty/Pack on pack-size SKUs come from Packaging. Prep Type often shows as (at checkout) under Pack cascade / notes - it still sets Tracker packaging when the order has a grind. Override Qty/Pack if needed, then Save changes.
